questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my German in a manner, so I can read academic articles in German. It was therefore crucial for me, that my destination was in a German speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It wasn't too easy to find out what courses were still relevant in the semester before maybe one month before semester start which is April 1st. But the course selection system is very 'loose', meaning that if you show up at a seminar and ask if you can participate you will most likely get a yes.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got a lot of links about where to get information, there were campus tours, and a specific tour for psychology students, where we were instructed in how to choose courses and where else we could fin information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I made a post on Instagram and a friend hooked me up with a place.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: When you pay your 'Semesterbeitrag' you pay for a Deutschlandticket, which is free public transport in all of Germany. So you dont have to worry about paying for transportation if you live a little off campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: A week after arrival you sign up for the classes yo wish to take, and then the day after you have a schedule. After that you can still show up at classes and ask if you can participate for another 2 weeks before your classes are final.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: the eramus mail was always answered quickly, and there was also a psychology specific one.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't worry too much about it before going. It is way more up to the teachers to decide if you can join a course/ class. If you show up at a class and ask if you can join, it is very possible that you can.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very interesting, but also more classroom focused than I am used to. Lectures are what you are examined in and not the curriculum.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took BA classes, that would be very appropriate to 4th semester of psycholgy in Cph as well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Examinations were based on the lectures given. Seminars has the same main theme as lectures but different focuses, so the curriculum was different and could vary a lot from seminar to seminar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Allgemein Verfahrenslehre der Psychotherapie, Berufsrecht und Berufsethik
- Pädagogische Psychologie
- Deutsch B2.1
- Karl Marx: Grundlagen einer Kritische Theorie
- Foucaults Denkwerkzeuge

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked Allgemein Verfahrenslehre, because there was a block-seminar of 3 times, where you practiced counseling. This was so fun and I really learned a lot.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay 308€ as a semester fee for online material, Deutschlandticket and some other things. But this is when you are enrolled.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Living is cheaper: Food is cheaper, cinema is cheaper, in general you spend less money on things.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports, clubs, extra lectures, cafés.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going to the cinema, its fun and cheap. Swimming pools are nice and especially the outdoor ones in the summer.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: You can go any German city with you D-ticket. Go to the pools.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. People are nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take courses in German.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were very friendly and they often really like Danes haha

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Go to PI-café
- The canteen is called Mensa and is really cheap and pretty good. 
- The system is not as fixed as in CPH so you can make a lot of things work they way you want to.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know new people and really improve my German

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Because the system is not as fixed, there are some thing you just have to trust will work out. This was a bit challenging, but it did work out:)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Berlin and FU is amazing. It might seem like a lot of work, but I had the most wonderful time. Go go go!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
